Class Tree.StringParser<L, NT extends L, T extends L>

java.lang.Object
io.github.ericmedvet.jnb.datastructure.Tree.StringParser<L,NT,T>
Type Parameters:
L - the type of labels of nodes
NT - the type of labels of non-terminal nodes
T - the type of labels of terminal nodes
Enclosing class:
Tree<L>
public static class Tree.StringParser<L, NT extends L, T extends L> extends Object

A parser which produces tree parsing strings. It has to be configured through four parameters (see the constructor):

  • a list of NodeParser for parsing labels of non-terminal nodes
  • a list of NodeParser for parsing labels of terminal (leaf) nodes
  • a BiPredicate for testing whether a given arity is acceptable for a given non-terminal label
  • a Configuration specifying parsing details, e.g., children separator For example, it can parse the string "a(b;c(d))" to the tree:
a
└b
└c
 └d

  • Constructor Details

    • StringParser

      public StringParser(List<? extends Tree.StringParser.NodeParser<? extends NT>> nonTerminalParsers, List<? extends Tree.StringParser.NodeParser<? extends T>> terminalParsers, BiPredicate<NT,Integer> arityPredicate, Tree.StringParser.Configuration configuration)

      Builds a new parser which will use the provided arguments for parsing trees from strings. The order of NodeParsers in the lists nonTerminalParsers and terminalParsers matter. The parser works recursively as follows (in parse(String)):

      1. it starts from the first character at index i = 0;
      2. attempts to parse a label at i using first the non-terminal parsers (in order) and then the terminal parsers:
      • if a non-terminal parser matches a label, it looks for a Tree.StringParser.Configuration.childrenStartDelimiter(), then parses inner nodes, separated by a Tree.StringParser.Configuration.childrenStartDelimiter() and terminated by a Tree.StringParser.Configuration.childrenEndDelimiter(); if it does not find a start delimiter, goes to next case;
      • otherwise, if a terminal parser matches a label, returns a tree with a leaf node labeled with the parsed label;
      • otherwise, throws a NoSuchElementException. When parsing label nodes, the parser permits empty spaces if Tree.StringParser.Configuration.allowVoid() is true.
      Parameters:
      nonTerminalParsers - a list of parsers for labels of non-terminal nodes
      terminalParsers - a list of parsers for labels of terminal nodes
      arityPredicate - a predicate testing whether a given arity (number of children) is legit for a non-terminal node labeled with a given label
      configuration - the configuration for this parser
